title: The Mandates Are Ending. The Pressure Is Not.
method: AI-assisted cross-source synthesis with direct links to originating publishers. Reviewed against a four-item gate including two primary institutional sources.

items.headline: Nyala market strike sends mass casualties to an MSF-supported hospital
items.whyItMatters: The hospital record establishes mass civilian harm even while the final toll and legal attribution remain unsettled. Repeated market strikes also disrupt access to food and supplies in a city already facing malnutrition.

items.headline: Somalia seeks a longer Ugandan troop presence
items.whyItMatters: A delayed drawdown could reduce the risk of a sudden security gap, but it would not solve the mission’s financing problem or establish a durable Somali replacement capacity. The extension request remains secondary reporting rather than a published bilateral agreement.

items.headline: United States sanctions Rwanda’s defence ministry and Zigama
items.whyItMatters: The action moves pressure from individual commanders onto a state ministry and a financial institution, increasing compliance risk around Rwanda-linked defence and banking activity. Treasury’s allegations are the U.S. government’s stated basis for sanctions; Rwanda’s response and any behavioural effect remain unresolved.

items.headline: Russia offers to mediate Ethiopia–Eritrea tensions
items.whyItMatters: Another mediation channel could create space for de-escalation around the Red Sea and the Ethiopia–Eritrea frontier. No formal process, mandate or acceptance by both parties was reported, and the arms relationship complicates the neutrality claim.
